newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Burns Philp sees unchanged yr result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Burns Philp sees unchanged yr result.

text.p: Spices group Burns Philp and Co Ltd said on Thursday that a competitive environment and higher raw material costs would constrain trading profits and that the full 1996/97 (July-June) year trading result would not be significantly different from that posted in 1995/96.

"The continued competitive environment and increases in raw materials costs are expected to constrain the increase in trading profits that will come from operational improvements," Burns Philp said in releasing its first half results. "However, the full year trading result is not likely to be signficantly different from that reported for the 1995/96 year," it said.
Earlier, Burns Philp announced a two percent rise in net profit before abnormals for the six months to December 31 to A$51 million, in line with market expectations.
Burns Philp said it improved operating cash flow by 48 percent to A$107.4 million, as a result of tighter working capital control, particularly in North America, and lower interst payments.
Clack said the company was not considering any further major business disposals or acquisitions.
"Our main focus right now is to get value out of the assets we own," he said.
